subject: general
question: If Mean > Median > Mode, then distribution is:
solution:
The correct answer is** positively skewed.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Positively skewed distribution:**

 
 
• In a positively skewed distribution, the tail on the right side (higher values) is longer or fatter than the left side (lower values).
 
• This occurs when there are a few exceptionally high values that pull the mean to the right, making the mean greater than the median, which in turn is greater than the mode.
 
• For a financial enterprise, this could indicate that while most data points (such as revenue or returns) are clustered at lower values, there are some significant outliers that are much higher, skewing the average.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Platykurtic distribution:**

 
 
• Platykurtic distributions are characterized by a lower peak and thinner tails compared to a normal distribution. This term describes the kurtosis of the distribution rather than its skewness.
 
 
 
• **Negatively skewed distribution:**
 
 
• In a negatively skewed distribution, the tail on the left side (lower values) is longer or fatter than the right side (higher values). Here, the mean is less than the median, which is less than the mode. This does not match the given condition of mean > median > mode.
 
 
 
• **Leptokurtic distribution:**
 
 
• Leptokurtic distributions have a higher peak and fatter tails compared to a normal distribution. This describes the kurtosis, not the skewness, of the distribution.
